about: Exact-output cases for the secret redactor. The launcher's SecretRedactor (src/Loadout.Core/Security/SecretRedactor.cs) and Studio's port of it are both held to this file, so a case added here has to pass on both sides. An input of null stands for no text at all.

cases.name: credentials in a remote url
cases.note: The most realistic leak: git repeats the remote in its errors.

cases.name: prefixed assignment with =
prefixed assignment with :
prefixed password assignment
prefixed assignment in lower case with spaces
authorization header
json credential field
known token shape on its own
ordinary diagnostic text
cases.note: Over-redaction is its own failure: a doctor report full of [redacted] is useless.
cases.input: git version 2.54.0; workspace synced; 12 projects registered
cases.expected: git version 2.54.0; workspace synced; 12 projects registered

cases.name: ordinary flags
no text
empty text
bare capitals keyword
cases.note: An environment dump writes TOKEN= with nothing before it.

cases.name: bare capitals keyword among other variables
bare capitals keyword with a capitals suffix
bare keyword after a PowerShell env drive
bare keyword in lower case is left alone
cases.note: Lower-case token= and token: are far more often error wording than a secret.
cases.input: token=abc; token: missing from the request
cases.expected: token=abc; token: missing from the request

cases.name: bare keyword with a colon is left alone
cases.note: The bare rule takes = only, so an error saying TOKEN: missing survives.

cases.name: bare KEY is left alone
bare keyword with a lower-case suffix is left alone
cases.note: The bare rule's suffix is capitals only, like the environment dumps it exists for.

cases.name: flag with a space
flag with =
flag with key after an underscore
flag with key as a separate word mid-name
flag with key as the last word of any name
cases.note: KEY after - or _ counts wherever it is, so --sort-key is redacted too; a flag is never ordinary error wording, so this costs little.

cases.name: flag with a long keyword anywhere, any case
bare --key is left alone
key inside a word is left alone
--monkey= stays redacted while --monkey with a space does not
cases.note: Deliberate. The older prefixed rule accepts KEY after any letter, so --monkey=abc is redacted by it; the flag rule takes KEY only as a separate word, so --monkey abc is not. Narrowing the old rule would loosen redaction everywhere.

cases.name: flag followed by another flag is left alone
single-dash flag is left alone
flag value on the next line is left alone
flag with a double-quoted value
flag with a single-quoted value
flag with = and a quoted value
prefixed assignment with a double-quoted value
prefixed assignment with a single-quoted value
bare assignment with a quoted value
unclosed double quote runs to the end of its line
unclosed single quote runs to the end of its line
unclosed quote stops before a carriage return
unclosed quote at the end of the text
backslash-escaped double quote stays inside the value
backtick-escaped double quote stays inside the value
doubled double quote stays inside the value
backslash-escaped single quote stays inside the value
backtick-escaped single quote stays inside the value
doubled single quote stays inside the value
escapes apply in assignments too
an empty quoted value
cases.note: A doubled quote is an escape only inside a value, so an empty pair closes at once.
